content: The Wayback Machine is the most important website nobody talks about. It's the only reason half the sources in this archive are accessible at all. Donate to the Internet Archive if you use it.
Reminder that 'this was debunked' without a link to the debunking is not a counterargument. It's a social move. Different things.
The DNS rebinding entry is up. It's a class of attack that's been sitting in the open for 17 years and most developers have never heard of it. If you run any kind of local dev server, read it.

ref.label: DNS Rebinding: How Attackers Weaponize Your Browser

content: There is a specific kind of person who shows up in every drama thread to say 'both sides' and then leaves feeling like they contributed something. They didn't. Neutrality about documented facts is not wisdom.

Added a timeline to the loot box hearings entry. Looking at it laid out chronologically it becomes obvious how comprehensively the legislative momentum was absorbed and neutralized. The hearings were the outcome, not a step toward one.

ref.label: The Loot Box Hearing That Changed Nothing

content: The internet felt different before 2012. Not better in every way, but different in ways that mattered. More uneven, slower, more personal. The homogenization is not accidental — it's the product of a specific set of design and business decisions made by a small number of people.
If a story requires you to ignore the sourced version in favor of the vibes version, that's information about the story.
GeoCities entry is up. The section on what was actually lost — not the number, the qualitative argument about which pages disappeared — is the part that stuck with me while writing it.
